reviews.review:
I simply adore this game. I absolutely love the artwork, the story, the songs and most of all the many different cute and interesting robots and I sincerely hope that the devs will make a sequel. I definitely haven't had enough of Buddy and Bag Boy and all of their friends! <3

It's a very casual game that aside from some darker parts of the story feels aimed at a younger audience. If you're looking for a challenge you won't find much of that here. The gameplay consists of exploring every nook and cranny of each level while collecting bits and bobs to help you progress in the story. Along the way you meet a variety of robot npcs to help out and there's a bit of simple combat too, but it's a very minor part. There are also some platforming elements, which for the most part is on the easy side. I am no big fan of platforming and yet I didn't struggle much at all UNTIL the final chapter - more on that in a bit.

The game features a chapter select menu, so you can replay any level to grab any collectables or achievements that you may have missed the first time. Or save the challenges mentioned below for after the story. Saving in level is done via totem-like bots, but there are several in each level and it only takes a few seconds to pop over to one, if you feel the need to exit the game mid-level. Otherwise the game automatically prompts you to save after finishing each level as well.

Each chapter has an optional platforming challenge. By optional I mean that you don't have to beat them to progress and complete the story, but you DO have to beat all of them, if you want all the achievements for the game. I found all of them very reasonable to beat except the last one. I really wish the final challenge at least had a midway checkpoint. I do not find it fun to have to redo 20..30..40 jumps just to get back to where I failed over and over again. I did eventually beat it simply because I was too stubborn to leave that one single thing unfinished, but I did NOT enjoy the process. Mainly because the sequence is just too long to have no midway checkpoint to continue from if you fail far into it. Sure someone who enjoys hardcore precision platformers would likely find it easy, but for an otherwise very casual adventure game having that last challenge be so punishing if you fail just feels out of place to me.

That is however the one single negative thing I have to say about the game. Aside from that the game is a 10/10 for me. It made me laugh and it made me cry, it made me care about all it's peculiar inhabitants and I kind of envy anyone who still gets to play it for the first time. :D I'd recommend it for anyone who enjoys feel good games that lets you connect with your inner child. If you enjoy games like A Short Hike, Smushi Come Home, Alba: A Wildlife Adventure or Lil Gator Game then this might be right up your alley too.
